title: Per-token fidelity slab explorer and heuristic guide
content:
Purpose and context:
This is a working note describing a small, slice-based spreadsheet and a set of lightweight heuristics for assigning quantization "slabs" to different request slices (by length, prompt pattern, and SLA). Goal: give product teams a quick numeric picture of 1) cost impact, 2) latency delta, and 3) expected fidelity (proxy: delta perplexity / task metric) for candidate quant modes: FP16, FP8, INT8, 4-bit.
content_2:
Why 'per-token slab' approach?
- Many workloads are heterogeneous: short chat messages vs long document generation vs embedding-heavy pipelines.
- Applying a single quant mode globally either wastes cost (FP16 when short cheap requests dominate) or risks quality (4-bit for high-attention contexts).
- 'Slab' lets us define bucketed policies (e.g., tokens 0-64 -> INT8, 65-512 -> FP8, 513+ -> FP16) or route by prompt tag.
- Spreadsheet simulates per-request token counts and computes aggregate cost/latency/quality trade-offs so we can tune slab cutpoints and routing rules.
content_3:
High-level spreadsheet schema (columns we expect in the sheet):
- slice_id (string): human name for the slice (short-chat, long-chat, doc-gen, rerank).
- sample_fraction (decimal): fraction of total requests belonging to slice (sum=1.0).
- avg_input_tokens (int).
- avg_output_tokens (int).
- prefix_cache_hit_rate (0..1).
- model_base_rate_fp16_ms_per_token (float): baseline per-token latency in ms for FP16.
- relative_latency_multiplier_by_quant (list): e.g. FP8=0.92, INT8=0.85, 4bit=0.75 (these are knobs).
- cpu_postproc_ms (float): non-inference overhead per request.
- cost_per_gpu_hour_fp16_usd (float): pricing for that instance class.
- tokens_per_gpu_hour_estimate (formula): derived using throughput estimates.
- quality_delta_by_quant (list): expected task metric delta vs FP16 baseline (e.g., perplexity +1.8 for INT8, +3.4 for 4bit).
- chosen_quant (enum): assigned slab quant mode.
- computed_columns: total_cost_usd_per_1m_requests, avg_latency_ms, aggregated_quality_delta.
content_4:
Representative sample rows (text table):
1) short-chat | 0.55 | in=6 | out=12 | cache=0.45 | base_ms=0.30 | multipliers: FP8=0.9,INT8=0.8,4bit=0.7 | cpu=8ms | cost_fp16=20/hr | quality_delta: FP8=+0.2%,INT8=+0.6%,4bit=+2.3%
2) long-chat  | 0.20 | in=20 | out=380 | cache=0.10 | base_ms=0.32 | multipliers: FP8=0.95,INT8=0.88,4bit=0.78 | cpu=12ms | cost_fp16=20/hr | quality_delta: FP8=+0.5%,INT8=+1.4%,4bit=+4.0%
3) doc-gen   | 0.10 | in=50 | out=1500 | cache=0.02 | base_ms=0.40 | multipliers: FP8=0.97,INT8=0.92,4bit=0.82 | cpu=15ms | cost_fp16=20/hr | quality_delta: FP8=+0.8%,INT8=+2.1%,4bit=+6.8%
4) rerank    | 0.15 | in=1 | out=0 (embedding pre) | cache=0.00 | base_ms=0.15 | multipliers: FP8=0.85,INT8=0.70,4bit=0.60 | cpu=5ms | cost_fp16=20/hr | quality_delta: FP8=+0.1%,INT8=+0.7%,4bit=+1.9%
Notes: the numbers above are illustrative and deliberately conservative for INT8/4bit quality penalties.
content_5:
Heuristic rules we prototype in the sheet:
- Short requests (< 64 output tokens) -> favor INT8 when latency SLOs are tight and regen cost matters; prefer FP8 if small quality lift needed.
- Long-token streaming (> 512 output tokens) -> default to FP16 or FP8 hybrid (FP8 for early tokens, fall back to FP16 for coherence-critical segments).
- High-sensitivity tasks (NLP eval > threshold, e.g., summarization ROUGE drop > 1.5%) -> force FP16/FP8 only.
- Rerank/embedding hotspots -> aggressive INT8 / 4bit allowed because downstream ranking is resilient and vector similarity tolerant.
- Cache-first routing: if prefix cache hits >= 0.6, can be more aggressive on quantization for remaining tokens since continuation is cheap.
- Multi-model fallback: if serving latency > SLO, switch to lower-quant fallback on a short time-window for throughput relief (can increase quality alerts).
content_6:
How latency calculations work (simplified):
- effective_tokens = input_tokens*(1-cache_hit_rate) + output_tokens
- inference_ms = effective_tokens * model_base_rate_fp16_ms_per_token * quant_multiplier
- avg_latency_ms = cpu_postproc_ms + inference_ms + network_ms_estimate (row-level knob)
- throughput -> tokens_per_second -> tokens_per_hour -> cost per 1M requests computed from instance cost and utilization assumptions.
content_7:
Quality modeling & conservative fudge factors:
- We don't have perfect upstream evals for every workload; spreadsheet accepts an experimental column 'observed_metric_delta_pct' populated from small runs (A/B) and defaults fallbacks use 'proxy_perplexity_delta' as an initial prior.
- Conservative: multiply observed or prior quality penalty by 1.25 for 4-bit and 1.1 for INT8 to account for worst-case prompt chains. Update after each canary.
content_8:
Sample decision outputs we expect from the tool:
- recommended_slabs: a short list of slab cutpoints (e.g., [0-64: INT8, 65-512: FP8, 513+: FP16]) with estimated savings (e.g., -34% cost) and expected median latency change (+3ms).
- risk_buckets: slices labeled 'low', 'medium', 'high' risk of user-visible quality regression.
- canary_plan snippet: percent traffic for canary, metrics to watch (perplexity, ROUGE, latency p95), rollback thresholds.
content_9:
Operational checklist for product/ops before rolling slabs:
- run micro-A/B on each slice with 10k requests or 2h capture (whichever >), capture task metric and p95 latency.
- confirm cost-savings for projected 30d volume with 95% CI.
- update rollout policy in console: add slab route rules and automatic fallback to FP16 on error-rate increase > 1.5x baseline.
- alerting: add quality-regression monitor keyed by route+model+quant-mode.
content_10:
Open questions / TODOs
- How to model non-linear quality degradation in compositional prompts? (i.e., quality penalty grows with output length). Need empirical data.
- Should we support token-position-aware quant (e.g., lower precision after token 1024)? Implementation cost vs benefit?
- Align pricing assumptions: dedicated vs hosted cost curves differ. Add a toggle to switch pricing basis.
- UX: export recommended slabs as JSON valid for Redwood routing API (proto example needed).
- Experiment backlog: run 1k A/B per slice on 3 representative customers; gather delta-perplexity and user-reported regressions.
content_11:
Quick experiment plan (owner + rough dates):

content_12:
Notes-to-self (informal):
- spreadsheet should have a 'sensitivity slider' to vary cost per GPU hour +/- 20% and show breakpoint where slab assignment flips.
- consider a small LLM eval harness to produce ROUGE/BLEU deltas rather than raw perplexity for more downstream-relevant signals.
- push final recommended slabs to product-ops for inclusion in the next Dedicated customer playbook if we can show >20% cost reduction with <1% quality loss.
notes: This is a working doc — take the numbers as placeholders. If you copy to another doc, maintain the 'per-token slab' wording to avoid confusion with existing 'quant-tradeoff' artifacts.
